AGNES.acting: Agnes regards the unfamiliar tutor with guarded curiosity, remaining composed as she opens the exchange.
AGNES.head: HEAD-NONE

WILL.acting: Will tries to appear polite and self-possessed, though his attraction and uncertainty make him slightly restless.
WILL.head: HEAD-NONE

beats.acting: Agnes's direct question puts Will briefly on the defensive as he searches for a suitable answer.
Hearing that Agnes has already heard of him makes Will self-conscious about the impression he has made.
The hesitation sends Will inward as he searches for a less revealing explanation.
Agnes lightly teases him to ease the awkwardness while testing whether he will retreat.
The teasing increases Will's embarrassment, but he makes himself continue.
Mentioning the bird shifts Will's attention toward the hawk, giving him a safer subject than his real reason for approaching Agnes.
At the mention of her bird, Agnes's attention moves to the hawk before she corrects his imprecise description.
Agnes turns her attention back to Will and crisply corrects him, amused by his lack of knowledge.
The correction brings Will's attention back to Agnes and leaves him visibly more self-conscious.
